newsitem.title: USA: H&R Block tax service margin slips.
newsitem.headline: H&R Block tax service margin slips.

text.p: H&R Block Inc said Wednesday the pretax margin for its H&R Block Tax Services Inc fell to 22.5 percent in fiscal 1997 from 24.4 percent in 1996.
Tax services revenues rose 20.6 percent to $906 million, while pretax earnings gained 11.6 percent to $204.3 million.

"While we're pleased with tax services' revenue growth, our margins slipped due to increases in three areas: bad debt associated with electronic filing; marketing expenses targeted at gaining new customers; and costs connected with the implementation of a...computerized bookkeeping and management reporting system," Frank Salizzoni, H&R Block president, said in a statement.
H&R Block shares were off 1-7/8 at 32-7/8.

Earlier, H&R Block reported earnings for fiscal 1997 of $47.8 million or $0.45 a share, down from $177.2 million or $1.67 a share a year ago. Earnings for 1997 were hurt by a $186.5 million pretax loss reported by CompuServe Corp, of which H&R Block owns 80.1 percent.
H&R Block International's pretax earnings rose 20.8 percent to $14.2 million, while revenues rose 6.9 percent to $87.5 million.

"For the second year in a row, our tax operations have posted double digit increases in key areas both in the United States and internationally," Salizzoni said. "This validates our strong belief that there is still growth potential in the tax industry."
Block Financial Corp's pretax earnings rose to $7.1 million in fiscal 1997 from $1.0 million in 1996 before one-time items.
